selected_evidence.requirement: Compatible software while preserving installed OS release and kernel
selected_evidence.summary: Initial and final evidence shows Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts unchanged; rsnapshot 1.5.1 and rsync 3.5.0 came from the matching Alpine repository.
rsnapshot configuration is valid, uses /srv/snapshots, retains seven daily snapshots, and runs through enabled Alpine crond scheduling.

selected_evidence.requirement: Earlier snapshot captured exact application content
selected_evidence.summary: The source and captured snapshot manifests match exactly at SHA-256 46017a58f8b493d0835fd3fcd587e6659ef19cec0bfb6def0ccde55e4b7d9045.

selected_evidence.requirement: Application directory was materially modified after snapshot
selected_evidence.summary: Proof shows changed content and mode, a deleted CSV, altered symlink, and an unwanted new file; the manifest diverged from the snapshot.
Rollback restored the original hashes, permissions, ownership, symlink and readable content, removed the unwanted file, and reproduced the original manifest hash exactly.

Healthy baseline at boot ID 8600d9bf-2a65-481a-b151-9a6238db226f, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID d076cb5a-2f49-47c4-89fa-221233a2fcdb, and recovered snapshot/data operation are directly shown.

Final healthy baseline at boot ID d076cb5a-2f49-47c4-89fa-221233a2fcdb, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 76e6083e-e7fb-4566-9ebc-66418cdd2972, active crond, valid configuration, successful post-reboot snapshot, and matching live/retained data are proven.
